title: CISA withdraws six free cybersecurity assessments for critical infrastructure
plain: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has eliminated six free cybersecurity assessment services that critical infrastructure operators relied on, citing budget cuts. Tatyana Bolton, executive director of the OT Cyber Coalition, said the cuts have forced CISA into a position where it can no longer

angles.claim: AI security assessments for OT environments now default to vendor tools, so procurement and validation of those tools becomes an AI governance task, not a security team side project.
angles.audience: AI engineering leads and CISOs at utilities and other critical-infrastructure operators
angles.rank_reason: Directly changes what AI engineering leaders must check before Thursday, since they now own vetting the AI-driven scanning and assessment tools replacing CISA's role.

angles.claim: Any AI system CISA used to help validate through free assessments is now unvalidated until the operator commissions an equivalent review itself.
angles.audience: AI engineering and platform teams running or exposing OT-adjacent AI systems
angles.rank_reason: Reaches the target reader and is actionable on Monday, but it is a narrower inference the article does not state outright, so it goes further than the source without full support.

angles.claim: Operators building AI-based anomaly detection for OT should not assume federal review will ever validate the model, so validation has to be built into the vendor contract now.
angles.audience: AI engineering leaders negotiating vendor and integration contracts for OT AI tools
angles.rank_reason: Useful and forward-looking but more speculative about contract terms than the first two, and slightly further from what the article actually documents.
